s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and syncope following alcohol ingestion, with a prolonged time course and significant cardiovascular findings
salient_findings: Recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after alcohol ingestion
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions on ECG
ST segment elevations and depressions in multiple leads
key_facts: Patient presented with recurrent abdominal pain and syncope
Symptoms occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion
Symptoms lasted 5-10 minutes
Syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
Patient has a history of hypertension
Patient has a history of smoking and alcohol overconsumption
High-sensitivity troponin I was normal
Serum potassium was normal
ECG showed high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ECG showed ST segment elevations and depressions in multiple leads
Coronary angiography showed 10% stenosis in proximal LAD and RCA

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after alcohol ingestion, along with ECG findings of ST segment elevations and depressions in multiple leads, are consistent with vasospastic angina, which can be triggered by alcohol consumption.

rejected.label: Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of alcohol overconsumption, the coronary angiography results and ECG findings do not support a diagnosis of alcoholic cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's Angina
rejected.why: Prinzmetal's angina is a type of vasospastic angina, but the term 'Vasospastic Angina' is more general and encompasses the patient's symptoms and ECG findings.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy with Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction
rejected.why: There is no evidence of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the provided case report.

rejected.label: Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Similar to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, there is no evidence to support a diagnosis of obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
